title: CBSE CLASS 7 — Biology | Vegetative Propagation
description: Subject-wise test on Vegetative Propagation (Biology) for CBSE CLASS 7. 25Q.
subject: cbse7-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of asexual reproduction where new plants are produced from vegetative parts like roots, stems, and leaves?

options.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of male and female gametes.
Vegetative propagation is a method of asexual reproduction where new plants grow from the vegetative parts (roots, stems, leaves) of the parent plant.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from one plant to another, which is part of sexual reproduction.
Fertilization is the fusion of male and female gametes, which is part of sexual reproduction.

questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is a method of asexual reproduction where new plants grow from the vegetative parts (roots, stems, leaves) of the parent plant.

questions.question: Which part of the Bryophyllum plant can produce new plants?

options.explanation: While roots can be involved in vegetative propagation, they are not the primary part of Bryophyllum that produces new plants.
Stems can be involved in vegetative propagation, but in the case of Bryophyllum, it is the leaves that are notable for producing new plants.
Flowers are involved in sexual reproduction and are not the primary means by which Bryophyllum produces new plants vegetatively.
Bryophyllum plants produce buds in the notches along the margins of their leaves, which can develop into new plantlets.

questions.explanation: Bryophyllum (also known as 'mother of thousands') plants produce buds in the notches along the margins of their leaves, which can develop into new plantlets.

questions.question: A gardener wants to grow genetically identical roses quickly. Which method of propagation would be most suitable?

options.explanation: Stem cutting is a common and effective method of vegetative propagation for roses, producing new plants that are genetically identical to the parent plant and growing relatively quickly compared to seeds.
Growing from seeds involves sexual reproduction and does not guarantee genetic identicalness to the parent plant.
Grafting is a method of vegetative propagation, but it is not as direct or common for roses as stem cutting.
Tissue culture is an advanced method of vegetative propagation, but for a gardener, stem cutting is more accessible and common for roses.

questions.explanation: Stem cutting is a common and effective method of vegetative propagation for roses, producing new plants that are genetically identical to the parent plant and growing relatively quickly compared to seeds.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a disadvantage of vegetative propagation?

options.explanation: No genetic variation is a disadvantage because it makes crops more vulnerable to diseases.
Susceptibility to diseases is a disadvantage because vegetatively propagated plants can inherit diseases from the parent plant.
Overcrowding can be a disadvantage in agricultural settings where space is limited.
Production of seedless fruits is often considered an advantage of vegetative propagation, allowing for the cultivation of desirable varieties without seeds.

questions.explanation: Production of seedless fruits (like bananas or grapes) is often considered an advantage of vegetative propagation, as it allows for the cultivation of desirable varieties without seeds.

questions.question: Potato tubers have 'eyes' from which new plants can grow. These 'eyes' are actually:

options.explanation: Roots are not the 'eyes' on a potato tuber.
The 'eyes' on a potato tuber are specialized buds that can grow into new plants.
Leaves are not the 'eyes' on a potato tuber.
Flowers are not the 'eyes' on a potato tuber.

questions.explanation: The 'eyes' on a potato tuber are specialized buds. When a piece of potato containing an 'eye' is planted, these buds sprout and grow into new potato plants.

questions.question: A farmer observes that his sugarcane crop, when grown from seeds, takes a very long time to mature and the quality of the cane varies. To ensure consistent quality and faster maturity for the next season, which method should he adopt?

options.explanation: Cross-pollination is a part of sexual reproduction and does not directly address the issue of consistency and speed in sugarcane production.
Self-pollination is also a part of sexual reproduction and does not guarantee the consistency and speed needed for sugarcane production.
Stem cuttings are a method of vegetative propagation that ensures new plants are genetically identical to the parent, leading to consistent quality and faster maturity.
Growing from spores is not a common method for sugarcane propagation and does not address the need for consistent quality and faster maturity.

questions.explanation: Sugarcane is commonly propagated by stem cuttings. This method ensures that the new plants are genetically identical to the parent plant, thus maintaining consistent quality and allowing for faster growth and maturity compared to growing from seeds.

questions.question: Which of the following plants is primarily propagated through its leaves?

options.explanation: Rose is primarily propagated through stem cuttings, not leaves.
Potato is primarily propagated through tubers, which are modified stems.
Bryophyllum produces new plantlets from buds on its leaves.
Onion is primarily propagated through bulbs, which are modified stems.

questions.explanation: Bryophyllum is well-known for its ability to produce new plantlets from buds located along the margins of its leaves.

questions.question: Consider a situation where a rare plant species is facing extinction, and scientists want to produce many exact copies of it quickly and efficiently in a laboratory setting. Which artificial method of vegetative propagation would be most suitable?

options.explanation: Layering is a method of vegetative propagation but is not as efficient or controlled as tissue culture for producing many exact copies quickly.
Grafting is a method of vegetative propagation but is more complex and not as suitable for rapid multiplication of a rare species as tissue culture.
Cutting is a common method of vegetative propagation but does not offer the same level of control or efficiency as tissue culture for rapid multiplication.
Tissue culture is highly efficient for rapid multiplication of rare or endangered species, producing many genetically identical plants from a small piece of parent tissue under controlled conditions.

questions.explanation: Tissue culture is an advanced artificial method of vegetative propagation where plant cells, tissues, or organs are grown in a sterile nutrient medium under controlled conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a plant that undergoes vegetative propagation naturally through its underground stem called a rhizome?

options.explanation: Potato propagates through tubers, which are modified stems but not rhizomes.
Ginger propagates naturally through a rhizome, producing new shoots and roots.
Onion propagates through bulbs, which are modified stems but not rhizomes.
Carrot propagates through seeds and has a taproot, not a rhizome.

questions.explanation: Ginger is an example of a plant that propagates naturally through a rhizome, which is a modified, horizontal, underground stem that can produce new shoots and roots.

questions.question: Which of the following is a method of asexual reproduction where new plants are produced from the vegetative parts like stem, root, or leaves of the parent plant?

options.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote.
Fertilization is the process of fusion of male and female gametes.
Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction where a new plant grows from a part of the parent plant other than a seed.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma.

questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction where a new plant grows from a part of the parent plant other than a seed (i.e., stem, root, or leaf).

questions.question: A plant like Bryophyllum can reproduce new plants from its:

options.explanation: While some plants can reproduce from roots, Bryophyllum is known for leaf reproduction.
Stems can be involved in vegetative propagation, but Bryophyllum is specific to leaves.
Bryophyllum reproduces new plants from buds on its leaves.
Flowers are involved in sexual reproduction, not the specific method used by Bryophyllum.

questions.explanation: Bryophyllum plants are known for their ability to reproduce vegetatively from buds that develop along the margins of their leaves.

questions.question: One of the main advantages of vegetative propagation is that the new plants produced are:

options.text: Genetically diverse from the parent plant.
options.explanation: Genetic diversity is a result of sexual reproduction, not vegetative propagation.

options.text: Slower to grow compared to seed-grown plants.
options.explanation: Growth rate is not directly related to the method of reproduction in this context.

options.text: Genetically identical to the parent plant.
options.explanation: Vegetative propagation results in offspring that are genetically identical to the parent.
Disease resistance is not guaranteed by vegetative propagation.

questions.explanation: Since vegetative propagation involves only one parent and no fusion of gametes, the offspring are exact genetic copies (clones) of the parent plant.

questions.question: A gardener takes a small branch of a rose plant, removes its lower leaves, and plants it in the soil to grow a new rose plant. This method is an example of:

options.explanation: Layering involves bending a stem to the ground and allowing it to root.
Grafting involves joining parts of two plants together.
Cutting involves planting a cut piece of a plant to grow a new one.
Budding is a form of grafting that uses a single bud.

questions.explanation: Cutting is an artificial method of vegetative propagation where a part of the stem (or root, or leaf) is cut and planted to grow a new plant.

options.explanation: Roots are not typically referred to as 'eyes' in potatoes.

The 'eyes' are nodes on the potato that contain dormant buds.
Seeds are not involved in the 'eyes' of a potato.

questions.question: A farmer has a mango tree that produces excellent quality, large fruits but grows very slowly. He also has another mango tree that grows very fast and is resistant to local pests, but its fruits are small and fibrous. To quickly produce many trees with large, good quality, pest-resistant fruits, which vegetative propagation method would be most suitable?

options.explanation: Stem cutting would not combine the traits of both trees.
Layering involves bending a stem to the ground and does not combine traits from two plants.
Grafting combines the desirable traits of two plants.
Spore formation is not relevant to combining traits in mango trees.

questions.explanation: Grafting allows combining the desirable traits of two plants: the scion (from the good fruit tree) provides the fruit quality, and the stock (from the fast-growing, pest-resistant tree) provides the robust root system and growth characteristics.
